assertions.text: Cell values use concrete domain terms, not abstract codes.

assertions.text: Column names use business language, not code identifiers.

assertions.evidence: 1 method(s) checked — no if/switch/ternary

assertions.text: Distinct concerns are each covered without a monolithic cross-multiplied table.

assertions.text: Age boundary, credit score categorisation, and income status are each covered by minimal scenarios.

assertions.text: Scenario names and @Description do not restate values already shown in table cells.
assertions.evidence: Description states policy thresholds ("credit score of 650", "lower threshold of 600") which are not fixed to one value shown in every row

assertions.text: Effect of stable income visible via a held-constant row pair with different decisions.
assertions.evidence: "Qualifying score with unstable income | 40 | 700 | false | REJECTED" vs "Qualifying score with missing income information | 40 | 700 | | PENDING_REVIEW" — same age/score, differing income and decision

assertions.text: The build file (build.gradle) includes org.tabletest:tabletest-junit as a test dependency

assertions.text: Cell values make the rule falsifiable, not merely distinguishable.
assertions.evidence: Result column varies across REJECTED, APPROVED, PENDING_REVIEW depending on inputs, not a fixed value or verbatim copy of an input cell

assertions.text: A reader can state the rule from the table alone, without the test method body.

assertions.text: Each @DisplayName (or fallback method name) states what the code under test does, not an external fact.
assertions.evidence: Method name `evaluatesLoanApproval` describes the evaluator's action, not a restated policy or domain fact.

assertions.evidence: Compilation succeeded

assertions.text: A value the rule's outcome depends on, held constant across rows, must be visible as a column or named in the title/description.
